name: Sodium
occurrence: Never found free in nature; abundant combined as rock salt (NaCl), and dissolved in seawater.
majorUses: Table salt and food preservation (as NaCl)
Heat-transfer coolant in some nuclear reactors
biologicalRelevance: The main positive ion outside your cells, essential for nerve impulse transmission and fluid balance — which is exactly why sports drinks and IV fluids contain it.
notableCharacteristics: Soft enough to cut with a knife and reacts violently with water, fizzing across the surface and sometimes igniting the released hydrogen.
whyHere: A single, loosely-held 3s electron sitting outside a stable neon core is easy to strip away, which is exactly why sodium so readily forms Na⁺ and reacts explosively with water to release that electron's energy.
didYouKnow: The characteristic yellow flame test colour of sodium is so intense it can mask the flame colours of other metals mixed in the same sample.
genZNote: Soft metal that absolutely loses it around water. Chemistry's go-to example of 'do not mix these two things.'
